content.title: About
content.content: Stuffed olives are olives, usually green or black, filled with various fillings such as cheese, nuts, spices, or meat pastes. They combine the characteristic salty flavor of olives with the aroma of the stuffing and are often served as an appetizer or used as an ingredient in dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Stuffed olives are popular in Mediterranean cuisine, especially in Italy, Spain and Greece.
Traditional fillings include feta cheese, anchovies, almonds, garlic and aromatic herbs.
Olives contain polyphenols that give them antioxidant properties.
In ancient Roman cuisine olives were often stuffed with spices and honey.
Stuffed olives are frequently used in cocktails, for example in a martini.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Olives provide monounsaturated fatty acids that support heart health.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Polyphenols and vitamin E in olives help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in olives promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Contains iron and copper
items.content: These minerals are involved in hemoglobin formation and energy metabolism.

items.title: Moderate sodium content
items.content: The salt used in brining can help maintain electrolyte balance, but should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Stuffed olives are often very salty, which can be an issue for people with hypertension.

items.title: Olive allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to olives or to the fillings.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some commercial varieties contain preservatives that may cause sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Olives are calorie‑dense due to their fat content, so they should be eaten in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Stuffed olives are served as a snack, added to salads, pastas, pizza, tapas and cocktails. They can also be incorporated into hot dishes such as casseroles or risotto to add flavor and texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep olives in the original jar or a sealed glass container in the refrigerator. Once opened, consume within 1‑2 weeks. Discard if mold, off‑smell, or taste changes appear.
